Record Class Ray

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
net.minestom.server.collision.Ray
Record Components:
origin - the ray's origin
direction - the ray's normalized direction
distance - the maximum distance the ray will check
inverse - the cached inverse of the ray
public record Ray(Point origin, Vec direction, double distance, Vec inverse) extends Record
A ray that can check for collisions along it.

You should construct a Ray using Ray(Point, Vec).

    • cast

      @Nullable public <S extends Shape> @Nullable Ray.Intersection<S> cast(S shape, Point offset)
      Check if this ray hits some shape.
      Type Parameters:
      S - any Shape
      Parameters:
      shape - the shape to check against
      offset - an offset to shift the shape by, e.g. for block hitboxes
      Returns:
      an Ray.Intersection if one is found between this ray and the shape, and null otherwise

    • cast

      @Nullable public <S extends Shape> @Nullable Ray.Intersection<S> cast(S shape)
      Check if this ray hits some shape.

      If you're checking an Entity, use cast(Shape, Point) with its position.

      Type Parameters:
      S - any Shape - for example, a BoundingBox
      Parameters:
      shape - the shape to check against
      Returns:
      an Ray.Intersection if one is found between this ray and the shape, and null otherwise

    • cast

      public <S extends Shape> List<Ray.Intersection<S>> cast(Collection<? extends S> shapes)
      Get an unordered list of collisions with shapes.

      If you need to know which collisions happened first, use castSorted(Collection) or Collections.min(Collection).

      Type Parameters:
      S - any Shape - for example, an Entity or BoundingBox
      Parameters:
      shapes - the shapes to check against
      Returns:
      a list of results, possibly empty

    • findBlocks

      public BlockFinder findBlocks(Block.Getter blockGetter)
      Gets a BlockFinder along this ray.

      This is useful if you need only the first hit point, for instance, as it does not perform merging.

      Parameters:
      blockGetter - the provider for blocks, such as an Instance or Chunk
      Returns:
      a BlockFinder

    • findBlocks

      public BlockFinder findBlocks(Block.Getter blockGetter, Function<Block, Collection<BoundingBox>> hitboxGetter)
      Gets a BlockFinder along this ray.

      This is useful if you need only the first hit point, for instance, as it does not perform merging.

      Parameters:
      blockGetter - the provider for blocks, such as an Instance or Chunk
      hitboxGetter - a function that gets bounding boxes from a block

      BlockFinder provides some options, and BlockFinder.SOLID_BLOCK_HITBOXES is the default.

      Returns:
      a BlockFinder

    • blockQueue

      public BlockQueue blockQueue(Block.Getter blockGetter)
      Gets a BlockQueue along this ray.

      These can perform merging. They are useful if you need exit points from blocks.

      Parameters:

      Returns:

      public final boolean equals(Object o)
      Indicates whether some other object is "equal to" this one. The objects are equal if the other object is of the same class and if all the record components are equal. Reference components are compared with Objects::equals(Object,Object); primitive components are compared with the compare method from their corresponding wrapper classes.
      Specified by:
      equals in class Record
      Parameters:
      o - the object with which to compare
      Returns:
      true if this object is the same as the o argument; false otherwise.
